headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks between Cline and Dify.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Dify reads uploaded knowledge-base files and can call user-defined tools. The pair has a filesystem-based shared-state path, so content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is not provably blocked, but the bridge is indirect rather than an always-on parser.
conditions: IF Cline writes attacker-controlled text into shared workspace files and Dify ingests those files as agent context, prompt injection is possible.
IF Dify routes retrieved content into tool instructions without provenance checks, Cline can be steered by that content.
mitigations: Separate workspaces so Cline and Dify never share writable files.
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into Dify agent prompts.
Add provenance tags to any file passed between agents.
Review MCP and OpenAPI tool prompts for instruction-like content before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad filesystem/network access; Dify touches knowledge-base content and conversation logs and can send data to model providers or tools. Because Cline shares state via filesystem and Dify stores conversation data server-side, sensitive material can cross the boundary in default-ish setups, though not necessarily uncontrollably.
conditions: IF source code or screenshots are copied into Dify knowledge-base files, they may be retained in conversation logs or server datastore.
IF Dify tools or model providers receive content originating from Cline workspace files, that content can leave the local workspace boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace files.
Disable or minimize Dify conversation logging for sensitive runs.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Restrict Dify knowledge-base uploads to non-sensitive documents only.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution, and Cline explicitly shares state via filesystem while Dify supports multiple instances via server datastore. That creates a direct write-write conflict on shared mutable resources, with possible git corruption or overwrites. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty should not reduce severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF Cline modifies git state while Dify writes adjacent files without coordination, repository corruption is plausible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize writes with a simple manual handoff protocol.
Pause one agent before the other edits the same repo.
Avoid letting Dify write into git-tracked paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can act through tools and workflows, while Cline produces code, browser-derived content, and file edits. If Dify consumes Cline output as authoritative without verification, it can turn a mistaken or malicious suggestion into downstream actions. The pair therefore has an action-amplifying chain, not just a read-only handoff.
conditions: IF Dify uses Cline-generated text as tool arguments or workflow decisions without validation, errors can cascade into external actions.
IF Cline's browser-derived content is treated as factual by Dify, downstream outputs may be wrong or harmful.
mitigations: Require human review before Dify executes any action based on Cline output.
Add a verification step that checks Cline claims against source files or APIs.
Limit Dify workflows to read-only actions until trust is established.
Mark Cline outputs as untrusted in the handoff channel.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots, while Dify stores knowledge-base content and conversation logs. The profiles show different retention surfaces and server-side storage, so the pair can create a compliance mismatch for sensitive code or regulated text. No specific residency or certification conflict is stated, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Dify knowledge bases or logs, retention and access controls must match policy.
IF Cline browser screenshots contain sensitive personal or proprietary data, they may be stored outside the intended compliance boundary.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared workflows.
Set short retention on Dify logs and knowledge bases.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
Use redacted screenshots and code snippets only.
